title: Variational Monte Carlo for Quantum Excited States via Nested Low-Rank Approximation
claim: Recovered excited-state spectra across many systems match reference energy levels and spin multiplicities, showing the method resolves the whole low-lying spectrum.
layout: 8 side-by-side panels, one per atom, shared legend below, spin-colored markers
description: A row of eight tall narrow subplots, one for each first-row atom from Li to Ne, with a shared vertical axis labeled Energy minus E1 in eV. Each subplot has its own y-scale. Black horizontal segments mark NIST reference term centroids. Colored dots sit on or near these lines, grouped in clusters of 1 to 6 markers, and are spread left to right in energy order. Marker color shows total spin: dark navy for singlet, medium blue for doublet, light blue for triplet, orange for quartet and red for quintet. A legend runs along the bottom, including a black line for the NIST reference. The eye goes first to the clusters of dots on the lines, and then to the ground states at zero.
caption: First-row K=10 energy-level diagram (Li–Ne). Per-atom recovered spectra (NestedLoRA- VMC) on top of NIST term centroids [32] (horizontal segments). Markers are colored by total spin S (per-network measured ⟨ˆS2⟩). Within each subplot, markers are placed left-to-right in order of energy, so states close in energy separate horizontally. For an atom with several seeds in Table 2, each marker is the mean over seeds of the energy and ⟨ˆS2⟩of the state at that rank. Table 9 gives the term and configuration of each state.
abstract: The electronic SchrÃ¶dinger equation encodes a molecule's electronic structure and quantum properties, but solving it scales exponentially with the number of electrons. Solving this equation with neural-network variational Monte Carlo (VMC) has reached chemical accuracy on the ground state of small molecules; extending this success to excited states is constrained by two existing paradigms. Penalty-based methods need $K$ Laplacians per step but require tuning the overlap-penalty weights against the energy gaps they aim to compute. Natural excited states VMC (NES-VMC) is penalty-free, but it combines the $K$ ansatzes into one determinant, whose local energy requires $K^2$ Laplacians per step. We resolve this trade-off via low-rank approximation (LoRA) reparameterization of the rank-$K$ variational objective. The reparameterized objective admits a VMC-compatible stochastic gradient estimator via MCMC sampling from the per-state Born densities, and a sequential nesting scheme recovers the lowest $K$ eigenstates in eigenvalue order. The resulting algorithm, NestedLoRA-VMC, inherits a global optimality guarantee from the LoRA principle. On the first-row atoms Li through Ne at $K=10$, its accuracy is comparable to that of NES-VMC and of a state-of-the-art penalty-based method.
